answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. The practical upshot is that honesty is the only strategy that scales — a farm that tries to game the system pays for each identity it adds.. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. Consider a quill as the anchor of the cost.
